Laptop Stand, MISOTT Ergonomic Adjustable Laptop Stand, 2 in 1 Computer Stand Tablet Stand, Stand for Laptop Compatible with 10-15.6" Laptops and Tablets(Aluminum, Silver) This stand is perfect for my needs as I do not plan to carry it around. In 2018, I ordered a [[ASIN:B07HBQSCM3 Boyata Laptop Holder]] and love it. It has been working well for almost 2-years of daily use with my 14" LG Laptop. The Boyata will hold up to a 17" laptop. However, I wanted another stand to use for my "smaller footprint" tablets, so I decided on this one.

First of all, this collapses to a compact footprint as shown in the first few photos. Second, there is no assembly required. It is stylish (I love the flame cutouts) and simple. It arrives in a collapsed state and takes some strength to pull apart and move it into a desired angle.

I can adjust this to the angle that is most comfortable for me. I can also use this to angle my screen and also use a separate keyboard and mouse (which I can store underneath when not in use). This fits my 14" LG Notebook, my 12.9" iPad Pro, and my 10.1" Fire Tablet. It is not suitable for devices over 14". Although the Amazon page says it will work with 15.6" laptops, I do not recommend it as my 14" laptop hangs over each edge by 2.5" each side.

The anti-skid silicone pads on the bottom ensure that this does not slip around on my desk. The open flame design provides an opening for air circulation so the device does not overheat.

Only time will tell if the "hinges" on this stand will last and not collapse. I suppose if one changes the position of the stand daily, that this may not be so sturdy. Nevertheless, so far I love it for my purpose as I will be using this with my 12.9" iPad Pro or other smaller tablets I have. If it should fail in any way, I will update my review.

In summary, I do feel this is a nice non-portable stand option for laptops or notebooks under 14". I would not put anything above that size on this despite what the Amazon site says. The current price of $34.99 minus 30% brings the cost of this stand down to $24.50 which is exceptionally reasonable considering my other stand was $50.
text_fidelity_b: Laptop Stand, MISOTT Ergonomic Adjustable Laptop Stand, 2 in 1 Computer Stand Tablet Stand, Stand for Laptop Compatible with 10-15.6" Laptops and Tablets(Aluminum, Silver)

RCA Compact Outdoor or Attic Yagi TV Antenna – HD Antenna with Super Long 75 Mile Range – Long Range Digital OTA Antenna for Clear VHF & UHF Reception, NexGenTV ™ Compatible, Supports 4K/8K 1080p TVs The trick with this antenna is not getting frustrated with moving it around and pointing it in the right direction. I mounted mine on the hand rail of my apartment balcony, second floor and now receive all local channels 4-68. Channel 68 being about 45 miles away. All are received in full green in windows media center, without using a preamp.

Previously I had it mounted under and bolted to the 3rd floor balcony to try and keep it out of sight. Reception was iffy on 4 favorite channels. I then moved it to its' present location with the idea that the antennas footprint is considerably smaller than all the satellite dishes mounted on balconies throughout the complex. The mounting bracket and pole that come with it, are the same type satellite dishes use, Very strong and versatile. You will need to buy some good bolts, I used 4, 5/16" x 1- 1/2" Galvanized Lag and flat washers, I predrilled 3/16" pilot holes first. I just thought I'd mention that for those not fastener savvy.

I would guess the antenna mount alone is worth 1/3rd of the entire antenna cost. Recommend a good quad shield coaxial cable with the thick, sollid copper wire. A shorter run is better if possible. I only have about 12 feet to my PC/TV.

Once I figured out how to mount this antenna correctly, a month ago, I haven't had to adjust it.
text_fidelity_b: RCA Compact Outdoor or Attic Yagi TV Antenna – HD Antenna with Super Long 75 Mile Range – Long Range Digital OTA Antenna for Clear VHF & UHF Reception, NexGenTV ™ Compatible, Supports 4K/8K 1080p TVs

text_fidelity_a:
3MP Wireless Security Camera System, Dragon Touch 8CH NVR 4pcs WiFi Security Cameras Outdoor with Color Night Vision, AI Human Detection, Motion Alert, Remote Access, IP66 Waterproof Cameras, No HDD Prior to getting this NVR system, I had already started researching on POE switches. For some reason, I assumed all NVR cameras are POE. I knew this Dragon Touch NVR had no POE ports in the back, but it didn't matter because I had planned to use POE switches. If you're a newbie like me, here are some noteworthy things before you make your decision:

1. The four cameras in this set comes with four power adapters. I thought how nice of them to include this option. But as it turns out, this is NOT an option. You need to use the power adapters for each camera. I learned that getting POE switches is only half the battle, the other half is making sure the cameras are POE compatible. I didn't know that. I thought POE switches would allow me to get rid of power adapters to any camera, any brand. Sadly, this is not the case. So this Dragon Touch system is designed for wi-fi. You only need to hook up the power adapter to each camera. But the whole point of me going to NVR is to use ethernet for more dependable connections. You can still do that with this system, but you'll still need to connect the power adapters, so you're running two cables for each camera. Had I known that, I would not have gotten this system.

2. You can use other brand cameras with this NVR if the cameras are ONVIF. However, I'm betting they still need to be the non-POE kind. I'm trying to connect a H.View POE camera, but I'm getting a black screen. Dragon Touch said that model is not compatible. End of email. I had to follow up with "What POE cameras are compatible?" I'll update when they respond.

3. It goes without saying, but in case you don't know, you need to connect NVR to a monitor for viewing. The back of the NVR has options for VGA or HDMI out. Alternatively, you can view via their Homeviz app.

4. No hard drive is included, but a hard drive is not necessary for you to start learning, testing, and setting things up. You can live view without a hard drive, but to record you'll need to install a hard drive.

5. Lastly, I'll talk about the build quality of this system. The Dragon Touch is very professionally packaged, the NVR is small and light, but that's without a hard drive currently. The cameras feel real nice, has good heft to them. I am not going to subtract any stars because of my newbie assumptions. As a matter of fact, I'm learning that if you want NVR systems with POE cameras, they would be much more expensive than what you're paying here. If I can figure a way to run both ethernet and power adapters, I may end up using this system. However, I will subtract a star for the lack of info in their listing, and emails. A product like this should clearly state whether or not their cameras are POE, and whether or not the NVR can handle POE cameras. 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: 3MP Wireless Security Camera System, Dragon Touch 8CH NVR 4pcs WiFi Security Cameras Outdoor with Color Night Vision, AI Human Detection, Motion Alert, Remote Access, IP66 Waterproof Cameras, No HDD

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch Immediately, I realized I love these headphones. I'm not in love with the color, and I'm perplexed why companies always say something is for iPad, etc., although I suspect it is just the "cool" thing to do. I have no apple devices, but this worked immediately and perfectly for my Blackberry 9700, Xoom, and Win7 Laptop.

The first device pairs by itself, and devices 2-8 pair by holding 2 buttons for 5 seconds. After that, if multiple devices are turned on when you turn the headphones on, it seems to want to pick the first one you paired it with.

The BB picks it up as a Logitech Wireless Headset (not something generic), and you can then control the volume with the BB or with the headset itself (Did I mention the controls are all well positioned on the right headphone? - just two volume buttons, mic mute, micro USB charging port, and LED indicator), and you can also toggle between BB speaker phone and headset - they are obviously fully compatible - not generically. Pressing the mute button give you an audible cue, but does not change the BB display.

You'll never catch me in public with a normal bluetooth earpiece on anyway, so this is also great for calls at home - it will cancel out more background noise (because of the foam on both ears) so you can comfortably concentrate on your call. My tests show it working well more than the claimed 10m away (of course that partly depends on the other device's radio as well).

As another reviewer said, these sound good (and are capable of getting louder than I'll ever need), but are probably not as great as the full over-the-ear headsets. BUT, the wireless capability is really great to keep you fully uninhibited when exercising, cooking, or whatever you're doing when talking on the phone or listening to your music. For the record, I am 100% opposed to wireless shelf/tower speakers in a real home system, but this is a great solution for a headset.

Also, the mic backing out of the way is a must, so thankfully that is included. It not only pivots, but flexes toward or away from the mouth as well - very good design. Finally, the folding feature is great; any space saved is important. And the connecting wire connecting the two sides is accessible, if all that bending ever has it in need of a replacement.

Past helmet use has me thinking my skull is about as large as they come, and these are comfortable on me with the sides fully extended.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch

text_fidelity_a:
Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I ordered the 'Geeni, Sentry Floodlight Security Camera with Motion Sensor, Intruder Alarm and Audio Video Recording' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I have had this camera for a while now and finally got it installed a couple of weeks ago and I am ready to share my thoughts and experience so far. This camera requires hard wiring which is why it took so long to get it installed. In my old home it was going to require me to get an extension cord, drill through my wall in the garage and plug it in, in the garage. This was much more work than I had anticipated. Now the new home already had normal motion sensor lights installed on switches, which made this more feasible for me to install. I took one of the motion sensor lights down and had to retrofit a new mount out of a piece of wood to cover the original hole left by removing the old light. This wasn't to hard to do and the Geeni light mounted with ease. Once installed and I turned the light switch on, it was ready to set up which took some time to do. I had to reset the device several times to get the App to set it up properly which was a quite pain however.

The camera itself is very good but so far I am not happy with all the notifications that I get which seem to be false alerts. It seems that everything seems to trigger this thing with absolutely no control as to how sensitive you would like the sensor to be. This is truly my main con with this device. I ended up turning notifications off on my mobile device which kind of defeats the purpose really.

Then there is the App which has thus far been pretty buggy. It has crashed many times and it is not so easy to find the "actual" activity that it seems to detect. Of all the motion activity that it detects, I would say that only 40% of it is relative. I do have the App set to just record everything (continuous) on the 128gb SD card which makes more sense seeing as there are so many false readings.

As for the good of this Geeni device, the image quality both during daytime and nighttime recording and playback is great. There is very little lag when accessing the footage which is surprising as I have other WiFi cameras that are painfully slow to connect and playback footage. This is probably my favorite feature (when the App doesn't crash).

Overall I do like this motion sensor and think that there is absolute value to it. I am however, really hoping for a firmware update which might help with some of the issues and allow you to adjust the sensitivity of the motion detection. Also it would be nice to have an easier way to track down and view "actual" activity rather than having to try and find that exact moment of capture. It seems to just tag a portion of footage, and you need to watch several minutes before you can find what it detected. You are also able to save the footage via the App, but doing so can take several days for it to show up on your mobile device which is another downside to this device.

I hope that this was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras Although this lens is intended for macro photography, it's also a great lens for general purpose shots, or portrait shots. The lens produces beautiful sharp images and is a fast, accurate focuser. The lens is moderately heavy and bulky, so I wouldn't classify it as eminently carryable, and without image stabilization, you might suffer hand shake blur if you're not shooting at the wide end; at smaller apertures, using it with a tripod is highly recommended. But if you're buying it primarily to get into macro this shouldn't much matter as tripod shooting with macro is virtually a necessity, and completely expected.

The 100mm focal length is a nice compromise when you want to get close to small subjects (particularly insects) but are limited to how close you can get before scaring the subject off - as a comparison with the 180mm macro, you would want to factor in a consideration as to what you might like to shoot most of the time - big spiders that you'd rather stay well away from might be an application more suited to the 180mm, for instance, but if you are keen to shoot mostly flowers, the 180 might be more length than you really need.

In short, the 100mm macro is one of my "keeper" lenses, a real performer.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..
text_fidelity_b: Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord

Cat8 Ethernet Cable 50FT, JEVIT Internet Network Cord, 40Gbps 2000Mhz LAN Wires, High Speed S/FTP LAN Cables with Gold Plated RJ45 Connector for Router, Modem, Gaming (15m/ 50FT） Keep in mind that since this has a PVC jacket, and since PVC produces toxic smoke, this shouldn't be run from room to room (per code) despite its long length.

Also keep in mind that cat8 doesn't do anything above cat6 unless you have a 10 or 40Gb/s NIC/SFP at both ends of your link, and the total link length is shorter than it was with cat6.

So unless you need a strong backbone link in a data center, don't think you need this.

If you are running a data center, you may want to look elsewhere: this cable appears to be hand wrapped. The connectors were pushed into the body of the roll in a way where the bend radius was dangerously close to being exceeded. I guess there's something to be said for buying the best if you're really using this for business.

Just know what you need and what you're going to do with it. For almost all home applications running from room to room, I'd take a cat6 cable with a legitimate riser or plenum rating any day.
text_fidelity_b: Cat8 Ethernet Cable 50FT, JEVIT Internet Network Cord, 40Gbps 2000Mhz LAN Wires, High Speed S/FTP LAN Cables with Gold Plated RJ45 Connector for Router, Modem, Gaming (15m/ 50FT）

text_fidelity_a:
Upgrade/RGB Video Light, 360 ° Full Color LED Camera Light, Dimmable 2500K-8500K Portable Pocket Size Camera Lighting, 12 Lighting Effect Mode, Built-in 3200mAh Rechargeable Battery We do jewelry photos which are very difficult to shoot, especially when iridescence is involved. We have big lights to set up and get good shots, but then we have been having issues with some of the light leaving things looking a bit dead. Enter this light. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This a light that is about the size of a smart phone- well the slightly larger ones. It comes with a case that has an elastic band on one side and a net bag with elastic top on the opposite side. The kit comes with a square slide to put on the camera along with screws to hold the discs in place to stop wobble. There is a charge outlet,, a charge cord (USB on the other end) and an output cord which goes from C to USB.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
When you turn this on, you press the power button and hold it down. The light goes on. There is a little window with the information in it.

TIME LEFT FOR USE
This tells you how many hours are left before you need to recharge so you can plan your sessions.

BATTERY
There is a battery indicator

BRIGHTNESS
From 5% to 100%

TEMPERATURE
Coolest temp being 5600K down to 3200K which is like candlelight.

DIAL
The dial on the side allows you to go up or down

POWER BUTTON DUAL MENU BUTTON
You use the power button to turn on the light, but once it is on, then if you touch it once quickly, it changes from brightness to temperature so you can set what you like. An arrow is very obvious so you know where it is set.

HOW TO ATTACH TO CAMERA
I have a Canon Poweshot G12 and this attaches up where a flash usually goes. You can screw this into the lamp either horizontally or vertically. You slide in the metal plate with the screw on it, then you screw the light onto that and use the discs to tighten up the light so it does not move.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I have to say, this little thing is amazing. It has fantastic light, works very well and even though you can use it by itself for video or interviews, etc, for jewelry photos, we need to have additional light to use with this to avoid shadows.

I have gotten some excellent photos which are really nice and with a little adjustments in photo editing turn out to be great in capturing texture, color, and iridescence.

CHARGING
I found that a few hours of charging gave me a complete charge. After using this for about three hours (I turned it off in between set ups) I still have four out of five bars on the battery indicator and about 4 hours left of predicted use time.

WILL I NEED ANOTHER LIGHT?
If you are doing product photos like we are of jewelry or something that is detailed and needs to have very good lighting, then you will probably need another light. I would say a second one of these would be perfect- set it up on a little tripod and it will be great. If you are just doing portraits, or interviews, you might be able to get away with just this light. Shadows at that point don't matter as much- unless they are severe, of course.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is one of the best things I have ever gotten for taking photos. It has really helped me take photos beautifully an I am thrilled with it. The temperature control is beautiful and the brightness controls are also excellent in increments.

MY RATING
FIVE VERY ENTHUSIASTIC STARS. This is a great portable light that goes with you anywhere. The case is great, and the light is the perfect size to toss into my camera bag when traveling.

PHOTOS
When I get some photos that I am not using on my site, I will try to post some for you. It is worth seeing.
text_fidelity_b: Upgrade/RGB Video Light, 360 ° Full Color LED Camera Light, Dimmable 2500K-8500K Portable Pocket Size Camera Lighting, 12 Lighting Effect Mode, Built-in 3200mAh Rechargeable Battery

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)

Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI) This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. I was so relieved when I got to the new place and just set my whole network up in an extra bedroom (until a proper telecomm closet can be brought online) and my Netgear Pro AP is doing a surprisingly great job. No problems keeping VPN connections up and no problems streaming video from my Plex server to the TVs. A lot less reconnect issues than you would have had even a few years ago.

There are plenty of slow spots for long range devices, especially in the basement and back yard. So I figured I'd try this as another interim solution to keep my new wiring project from becoming too pressing. Again, I'm truly surprised how well this works without having created any new issues for me. I had to use the app because my AP doesn't have WPS and I wasn't immediately certain whether this would have an IP address or not. But I got it up and running and just let it alone...surprisingly seamless.

All this WiFi will never be enough to satisfy me for the long term, but having a network that basically works right off the bat with barely any work involved has been a huge relief in getting settled in to the new place.

Oh, and I like that there is a network port on this. Obviously, that isn't a full solution, but taking out any piece of the wireless puzzle is always a step in the right direction.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR WiFi 6 Mesh Range Extender (EAX15) - Add up to 1,500 sq. ft. and 20+ Devices with AX1800 Dual-Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1.8Gbps Speed), WPA3 Security, Smart Roaming

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S) howdy y'all,

i bought this mouse to replace my logitech mx1100 cordless mouse. that one finally had the left mouse button start doing the dreaded false double click. it lasted several years, so i was not seriously annoyed. [*grin*]

for those coming from an mx1100, here are differences i noticed ...
- the mx1100 had the hump in the center instead of towards the back, so the main mouse buttons were shorter
this makes the mouse seem really rather too long. i am unsure if that will bother me once i use the new one for a while.

- the mx1100 had less of a slant to the right so that my hand sat a bit closer to level
the new one is more comfy for my very right-handed self.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel projected a tad more
combined with the sharp slant, the new mouse wheel feels like it is tilted the wrong way. it isn't, but i keep finding my finger on the right edge of the wheel instead of directly on the wheel.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel had a more pronounced side-move feel
the new mouse is very subtle. i liked the distinct feel of the older one when it toggled the side-move "button" function of the mouse wheel. of course, i like clicky keyboards, too ... [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had the upper thumb buttons just below the upper left edge
the new mouse has them on a surface that slants very sharply down to the left from the left edge. it makes the reach to the forward/back buttons a tad less comfy. combine that with a taper on those two buttons and i have found myself looking to see where the darned buttons went. they are also a tad more to the front of the mouse.
these admittedly annoying things that will likely fade out of my attention with use.

- the mx1100 used two AA rechargeable batteries
the new mouse uses one. since i use a lot of battery powered devices, i have a battery charger and several spares on hand. that means i will likely not use the usb charging function very often. still, one AA is better than having to charge two! [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had a larger usb wireless adapter
the new one is quite tiny! it works well - i put it on the back of my system among the tangle of wires that connect to other things and have had no reception problems.

*****
the parts list says there otta be a driver cd included. _not_ so! [*sigh ...*] you are referred to their download site if you want to use any of the extended functions or buttons. the performance mx has a $100 recommended price and there is no excuse to cheap out like that. thankfully, win7x32 has basic mouse support for the standard buttons, the mouse wheel, and the back/forward buttons.

this is a /_serious_/ fubar and i almost subtracted a star from my rating because of it.
*****

i suspect that folks with short hands will have problems with this mouse, but i am getting used to it already. i'm 6'1" and my hand is 7.5" from base to middle finger tip. not a _large_ hand, but not short.

*****
rated a THREE since it does what i expected - no more and no less. still, i came very close to rating this a two for not including the cd.

take care,
lee
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S)

Michael Kors Men's & Women's Gen 6 44mm Touchscreen Smart Watch with Alexa Built-In, Fitness Tracker, Sleep Tracker, Heart Rate Monitor, GPS, Music Control, Smartphone Notifications I have used smart watches for a while now and I have seen a steady progression in the technology. This is my first Gen 6 watch. It is a big improvement from what I have used before (beyond just battery life) and so far I am pleased with it.

This is an Android-based smart watch, and it is similar in interface to previous smart watches I have seen and used. If you have used any generation of smart watch before this one the experience is very similar. I won't get too deep into the nuts and bolts of that or the WearOS app.

There are two big areas of improvement I have seen with this new watch. First, the battery life is much better than previous smart watches I have used which is very encouraging. I have a Gen 2 watch that I love but it lasts only about 3 days on a charge, and my Gen 5 is not much better. This one lasts several days before the battery runs out.

The more important improvement to me, though, is the way it doesn't interfere with the Bluetooth in my car. Previous watches messed up my ability to stream to the car's sound system to the point that the sound would sputter and simply die. I did trace it to the watch by powering off the watch completely after which the problem went away and would come back when the watch was powered on. This watch does not interfere at all and my car's Bluetooth works whether the watch is on or not.

This is a stylish watch, a bit more upscale than some of the others I have seen and used. The band is a non-stretch link band that is a little snug but not unworkable.

So far this watch works well for me. I am pleased with the improved battery life and even more happy that it doesn't mess with my car's Bluetooth connectivity.
text_fidelity_b: Michael Kors Men's & Women's Gen 6 44mm Touchscreen Smart Watch with Alexa Built-In, Fitness Tracker, Sleep Tracker, Heart Rate Monitor, GPS, Music Control, Smartphone Notifications

Onkyo DXC390 6 Disc CD Changer,Black In a word, sound quality (OK, two words). If you have anything other than the most basic, low-end audio system, you will hear the difference in sound quality when listening to a CD on the Onkyo versus a DVD player. Highs are crisp, bass is solid without being muddy.

The unit itself is solid, and offers the ability to hold 6 CDs (and shuffle play). The changer works well -- no glitches so far after a few weeks of heavy use. Nice styling with an easy to see display. The buttons on the unit are a bit hard to see, but you'll quickly figure out what controls what.

The remote is not great, but decent. Good range so you can control disks from across the room. The buttons are rather small and don't provide much tactile feedback. I'm using this with an Onkyo receiver, so it can take advantage of the Onkyo interface (i.e., power up the CD player and the receiver automatically powers up as well and changes the input to CD). Only two cables to connect -- an optical out and the Onkyo interface cable.

The size is somewhat imposing (both height and depth). As other reviewers have mentioned, check the size specs before you buy to make sure it fits into the cabinet/rack you want to use.

Very happy with the performance, and find this to be an excellent value. Well worth the price!!
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo DXC390 6 Disc CD Changer,Black

text_fidelity_a:
SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V Here are my thoughts about Roku. Generally I like the product, but in setting it up I had some concerns.

PROS:
**Easy to set up
**Compact - it's so small it fits in one hand.
**Picture quality is pretty sharp depending upon the source. It is not HD quality but more like a decent DVD (though not Blu-Ray).
**A number of free channels available through Roku. You can add a lot of content. Since I'm an old movie buff, I added Pub a Hub (public domain movies) and Crackle (pretty bad recent movies but some good classics, like Easy Rider).
**Picture is big. I have a friend who has a projector that's five times as big as the Roku, and yet the projected image is the same size. That's impressive.

CONS:
**How much radiation does this device emit? In the fine print, the instruction booklet reads: "This equipment complies with FCC radiation exposure limits set forth for an uncontrolled environment. This equipment should be installed and operated with minimum distance 20CM between the RADIATOR AND YOUR BODY."
Hmm. I don't know about you, but it's hard not to sit pretty close to the projector. I used it in the bedroom and watched a movie on the ceiling. Of course I had to be close to it in order to put it at the right angle. How much radiation is the device emitting?

**Roku asks for your credit card information before you can use the device. When you set up an account, even if you don't want anything other than the free channels, they force you to put your credit card on file. The other privacy issue I object to is the way Roku allows you to connect to Facebook. In order for Roku to work, you were pretty much forced to allow Roku to access your information on Facebook at any time (even when you're logged out!) Not happy about this.

**In order to add some channels to the Roku network, you have to establish separate accounts. That means establishing one for Netflix, one for Amazon, etc, if you don't already have one. This means I'm sharing my account information with a number of companies I may or may not want to do business with. No doubt all this information will be shared among the video providers. That means a lot of spam will be coming my way in my email.

**Roku is geared toward convincing you to subscribe to as many streaming (pay on demand) services as possible. I'm not sure I would pay $300 for it, as it is very much a device aimed to getting you to subscribe to streaming channels. You can use it other ways, but Roku feels like a product sponsored by many vendors, as opposed to a stand-alone projector.

My conclusion? I recommend it with some reservations as noted above.
text_fidelity_b: SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V

text_fidelity_a:
GoPro Hero — Waterproof Digital Action Camera for Travel with Touch Screen 1080p HD Video 10MP Photos NOTE: There are several models of GoPro cameras attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the GoPro Hero.

I have worked with a number of the cheap knock-off sport cameras available and up to this point I have been relatively satisfied with them. I have not worked with an actual GoPro before now, so I was interested in seeing how well this unit would compare to the cheap clones. There’s really no comparison – the GoPro is an order of magnitude better. Yes, it’s more expensive but it’s a higher quality product that works better.

Of the GoPro models available, this is the most budget-friendly I have seen and it doesn’t come with a lot of frills and extras. It does come in a waterproof shell and it does have a clip so you can attach it to a helmet or handle bars, but that’s really about all that comes in the package. There’s no memory card with it, either, so plan on picking up a MicroSD card with the camera.

The usability when compared to the cheap clones is about the same. The menus are a bit different but they do perform the same general functions. That said, where the GoPro Hero sets itself apart from all of those cheaper cameras is in the quality of the product and the resulting pictures and recordings. This little camera is solid and so is the waterproof shell; it will stand up to some abuse and should just keep right on going without batting an eye. It also produces better-quality video than every clone I have tried, which is saying something because some of the cheap cameras actually do a decent job of producing good video.

The size and weight are nice features that make it very highly portable. I have seen motorcyclists on the highways with cameras similar to this one mounted on their helmets, and while that looks funny to the observer it makes for some great videos online and it does give the motorcyclist some backing when there is a traffic incident. For the younger crowd, it’s great for capturing skateboarding tricks in the first person as well as that wild ride down a water tube.

I have not worked with this camera a whole lot yet but I have seen enough to know it’s a big upgrade from the cheaper clones that are available in abundance. The Hero is a budget-friendly option for the user who wants quality results without breaking the bank, in exchange for giving up some of the less critical features like Bluetooth and WiFi connectivity. If you need those features, but you still want the best-quality, you’ll need to look at one of the more advanced and expensive models.
text_fidelity_b: GoPro Hero — Waterproof Digital Action Camera for Travel with Touch Screen 1080p HD Video 10MP Photos

text_fidelity_a:
GorillaPod Video Tripod (Black/Blue) The Gorillapod Video Tripod (Black/Blue) is a good idea on paper but in real life it just doesn't quite measure up.

The pan & tilt head is incredibly stiff which leads to jerky motion and bounce in your video. There also, on mine at least, appears to be a good bit of free play or slack in the vertical movement of the control arm. I've tried to tighten this down to no avail. The mounting screw seems to be a bit long. It wasn't bad mounting my RCA Small Wonder video camera but when I mounted my Kodak still camera the screw bottomed out and left the camera loose on the mount. The mount itself seems quite secure tight and sturdily attached to the tripod.

I like the adjustability of the legs but if you're not using the tripod on a metal surface for the magnetic feet to cling to it tends to just slide around when adjusting the pan or tilt. The magnets do appear to be strong for their size and will hold my RCA Small Wonder video camera fully horizontal on the 'fridge or door of my car. I tried this with my Kodak Z-650 still camera and it was too heavy for the magnets to support.

While on the subject of the magnetic feet I wanted to add a warning that if you're using an older CRT style monitor care should be taken to keep this tripod several feet away from your monitor. Even being more than a foot away from my 19" CRT cause distortion and image warping. There is the potential for damage to CRT monitors.

As a stationary camera mount this is a pretty cute product; easy to carry, lightweight with near infinitely adjustable legs. If you just want to plop down your camera so you don't have to hold it this product works fine. When you bring the flaws of the pan and tilt features into play the enjoyment goes downhill fast.

All in all it's not bad but it really isn't great.
text_fidelity_b: GorillaPod Video Tripod (Black/Blue)

Srhythm NC35 Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.0, Fast Charge Over-Ear Lightweight Headset with Microphones,Mega Bass 50+ Hours’ Playtime I want to point out up front, for those who are afraid these will be too big for a small head, that they fit me fine. I have a small head. I am a short woman, I have little ears, a little head. When these headphones are adjusted to be fully contracted, even without doing any bending of the top part, they fit great. They are lightweight but substantial, very comfortable, and I can see myself listening to them for hours without discomfort. I can lean back in my recliner without anything touching the headphones.

I didn’t know about the whole thing about burning in headphones. I’ve spent the last few hours down that rabbit hole, with all the opinions pro and con, etc., and I’m glad I’m doing it because I can already tell the headphones are responding to the burn-in process. I went to Spotify and looked for burn-in playlists, and I’m playing through one of them now.

I will not use these for noise cancelling, so I cannot comment on that. I want headphones that don’t bother my ears during hours of listening, that give me a clean, clear experience of the dynamics of the music, and that seem to become a part of me. So far, these are doing that. When I first started listening, I could tell these headphones were a little stiff and muddy, but they are loosening up now and becoming quite wonderful. I’m very pleased. And I’m only a few hours into the burning in.

Update: I just tried the ANC button. I’m sitting here, still in burn-in, watching the news on TV and periodically checking in to be sure the burn-in playlist is still playing. I could hear the TV when I was listening to Alice in Chains, and then I turned on the noise cancelling/ANC switch. Hey, this noise cancelling works pretty good! Of course, you get more pressure in your ears with ANC turned on, so it’s not a mode I would listen in for very long, but it definitely cancels the noise. Can’t hear a thing from the TV now. Flip the ANC switch, and I hear the TV. Flip it again, and there’s no voices coming through from the TV.
text_fidelity_b: Srhythm NC35 Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.0, Fast Charge Over-Ear Lightweight Headset with Microphones,Mega Bass 50+ Hours’ Playtime

Two things that I don't love: One is that the sliding mechanism that opens out to allow you to put the cords in and use the diagonally-sliding plugs easily - they are a little stiff. The other thing is that there is no method for hanging this outlet on the wall. So I have to set it on a high shelf, which is less cool than just hanging it behind my printer or something.

Otherwise, I love that I can neaten up a decidedly un-neat portion of my office with this, and be assured of clean power to boot.

text_fidelity_a:
Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black I run during the summer and run outside. I hate carrying heavy items with me, like water bottles and phones. I feel they sort of hinder my performance, though I realize it's probably more psychological than physical.
Still, I'm not going to mess with a run I've been accustomed to for nearly twenty years, but I do wish, more often than not, that I had some way of tracking my run and how many miles I've done *exactly* while being outside. Sure, I can track the mileage by checking my phone before and after, but it would be nice to have a tracker on me without adding any psychological weight. I used to have a Polar watch that worked fine, but it died some time ago and I never bothered to get a replacement.
But finally I did.

With this one, I'm able to wear the watch without toting my phone along and it still carries all the features and tracking as if the phone were connected to any other tracking watch. While this watch is used for a number of cardio activities, I use it only for running. There are "pages" of exercises you can track, but for a quick run the default is set on the bottom left button--very nice to have, especially for me. Not sure if you can change the default on there to another exercise, but for me it's perfect and I haven't bothered looking up how to change it.
But curious to check out the full features, I ventured into the different pages (or screens) the watch has to offer. During my course, I found that the buttons were *very* stiff. This might be to prevent accidental presses during exercise, but I found that I had to press almost twice has hard as other electronic watches for the watch to recognize my press. But, from my uses so far, I've pressed it mostly to view all the screens when testing out all the features. When actually running, I do no more than a few presses before and after each run. The network had trouble activating itself in the beginning, but that's because I was fiddling with it outside. It kept trying to set itself numerous times when I actually ran outside, but I always dismissed it. Once, however, I was under the open sky I let it connect and it has had no problem or delay connecting ever since.

After every run I am able to sync it with the Epson app, as well as RunKeeper. People have complained about the Epson app but I find it neat and useful.

Overall, it's a great little watch that accurately records my runs and uploads them without the use of the phone during the workout. I'm able to review it speedily on my phone right after, and I love that I can now track my progress without the burden of added weight. It's pricey for sure, but considering I don't need my phone and my previous watch lasted me ten years, I'm sure this watch will be a great investment that will last me hopefully for another decade or so.
text_fidelity_b: Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Divoom Pixoo-64 - WiFi Pixel Cloud Digital Frame with APP Control,64 X 64 LED Panel Display Frame for Gaming Room Decoration/Social Media Fans Counter THE GOOD:
--------------
* High quality, and very professionally manufactured.
* At it's most basic function, it is simply an animated picture frame, and the images are stylized to look pixelated.
* Downloading the app, Divoom, and setting things up was pretty self explanatory and intuitive.
* USB-C power port, which means no worries about which way the cable plugs in like the hassle of micro usb cables.
* Hang or use the included kick-stand.
* Overall, just something really fun to play with. A conversation piece for sure.

THE BAD:
------------
* Social media and game linking are very limited. My son would go bonkers if we can somehow link Roblox. There is Fortnite though. He doesn't play that as much, but we were able to link Fortnite, and it showed his stats.
* The screen doesn't really pop as much as I'd like. It's decent, but it would be nicer if it was brighter.
* It's covered by two film protections, full of bubbles. There should have been some easy lifting tabs. There are no lifting tabs, and the films run right up against the bezel. Making it extremely difficult to lift an edge. You feel like you're scratching the screen just trying to lift this film. I got the top film off. The second film was too difficult, so instead of lifting the second film, I just took a credit card and straighten out all the bubbles, and kept it as a screen protector.

Overall, I'll go 4-Stars for this nifty piece of tech.

text_fidelity_a:
Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More Ok, so I have to admit at first I was wondering why someone would spend this much on a Bluetooth headset that isn't a feature-rich entertainment one like those from Sony or a major fad brand like Beats, both of which I have some experience with. But this, no... this is actually something different. This is a serious tool for serious use with serious built quality and seriously useful features. Seriously.
For example, the telescoping mouthpiece means you'll get unparalleled mic quality compared to headsets that pick the mic up by your ears (looking at YOU, airpods!), both in clarity and isolation from background noise. You can also physically bend it out of the way, or use the button on the mic itself to mute. Try doing that with airpods. Then there's the button based features. Shortcuts and touch-sensitive buttons are cool on aesthetic devices, but the physical controls on this are an ergonomic user experience DREAM. Everything is easy to access and control, no apps or press-and-hold or counting LED blinks, etc. Sort of makes me miss the old days of phones with physical switches and buttons. When you want your equipment to get serious, this is the sort of user experience you expect. Then there's the charging rack. OMG I love that, I can store it on my desk and it's charging automagically. Pick it up and put it on, ready to go. Never needs to be charged because it's been charging in between uses. Finally, I'm really impressed with the USB dongle option. You see, the one thing I really dislike about wireless headphones is that you usually need to pair it with a device, then unpair it to switch to another device. For example, using my Sony headphones on my phone and tablet, if my wife wants to borrow them for a zoom meeting, I need to pair with her device but then also unpair with mine so that it doesn't keep trying to reconnect to it. Sometimes we just give up and use a wired headset to avoid that mess. Non-bluetooth wireless headsets have a dongle, which makes it easy to swap what you are connected to (no unpairing needed, just move the dongle) but then you can't connect to devices without a USB port like a phone. This is the best of both- you can pair it with your phone, but ALSO use the USB to quickly connect with your desktop or laptop without going through the process of pairing and unpairing. This is the kind of usability and professional quality I would expect from a brand like Plantronics, and all the while it works well as a stereo headset for music/gaming/etc as well. Very comfortable to wear for long hours, I'd highly recommend it for serious users.
text_fidelity_b: Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More

Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black) Trying to decide if we were ready to cut the cord, we installed this antenna to see if we could get all the local channels. We got 40 digital channels about 20 miles west of Washington DC and the major networks are crystal clear.

The network towers we use are clustered together about 20 miles away. We have 2 or more topographical obstructions between our house and the towers (no line of sight). The Noise Margin on the networks is 35-40 dB. TVFool.com listed my location as "yellow" (which means use an attic antenna or higher). The cable drop is about 25 feet and I did not use an amplifier.

This antenna is supposed to be omni-directional but we did experience occasional signal drop on the networks with the initial "eyeball" installation (which was off about 15 degrees). Standing directly under the antenna and looking through a compass I had my son walk through the yard until he stepped into the path to the towers. Then I had him stand still, facing the antenna, and rotated it until he told me it was pointed straight over his head. That seemed to fix the signal drops. Given all the factors of our situation, I am probably maxing out the performance of this antenna. If I have any issues I'll just buy the add-on the reflector shield to increase directional performance...but for right now I don't need it.

Installation was easy (I just mounted it to the Direct TV mast). This antenna is small and light which was a big plus when climbing up a 25 foot ladder.

So far so good!
text_fidelity_b: Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black)

Leather Laptop Messenger Bag for Men - Handmade Laptop Briefcase Satchel by Leather Centric I prefer messenger bags to backpacks so I selected this bag for myself to go with my laptop. I prefer leather to canvas bags, so this one is a good fit for me. There is one thing about this bag I would change, but otherwise I am pleased with it.

The leather used for this bag is something I have heard referred to as "distressed" or "ruined" leather, though neither are indicative of quality but instead refer to the appearance. It is made to look battle-worn and older than it is, but it's actually in very good condition. I looked this bag over for issues - loose stitching, cuts and tears in the leather, uneven seams and the like, and I found nothing. Overall, this is a well-made bag that has been assembled with some care.

The main compartment is divided and is large enough to handle my laptop as well as a couple of books. I have been able to cram in a few accessories as well and still close the zippers and closures without issue.

The main flap folds over the main compartment and uses a pair of snaps to fasten the flap down. The snaps are hidden behind false, decorative buckles. I am no fan of the type of fastener that was used, as I have had those break unexpectedly when I have caught the strap on something without realizing it. I would have preferred either a magnet which would break away easily or a real buckle which would hold tighter.

I like this bag and expect it to last for years to come. It looks great (if you like the "ruined leather" style) and it is made very well. The one thing I could change is the flap fasteners because of past experiences, but otherwise I have no complaints.

Logitech 910-000253 VX Nano Cordless Laser Mouse Retail Logitech says that their products are designed to move you, and this mouse sure lives up to that promise. Seconds after opening the beautifully packaged box, I was up and running and you can do it too. The instructions tell you everything you need to know, from how to put in the batteries (2 x AAA, included), how to turn it on (power button on the bottom), and where to insert the Nano receiver (USB port). For more features, Windows users can install the software included, and Mac users can go get the download.

Installation takes quite a few minutes, but once that's over, your mouse gets super powers, and can scroll from side to side (perfect for those extra wide pages), help you search the internet with the push of a button, and also navigate backwards and forwards between internet pages. How cool is that?

Here's all the OTHER good stuff about the VX Nano:

1. It's cordless
2. It's compact and cute, and oh so ergonomic (at least for small hands)
3. The MicroGear Precision Scroll Wheel (fancy name for the wheel thing between the buttons that you scroll with) has two modes: Hyper-Fast, for when you need to scroll down long documents at warp speed, and Ratchet, for when you don't have a long, long way to run. You switch between them by simply pressing down on the wheel. (Tilting the same wheel left or right gives you the side by side scrolling once you've installed the software)
4. There's a LED light to tell you when your batteries need changing
5. There's a compartment at the bottom of the mouse to store the Nano-receiver securely. Alternately, you can just leave the little thing attached to your notebook USB port.
6. The package includes a nice Logitech zippered case to keep your mouse snug as a bug in a rug.
7. You can use it on your desktop machine too. It comes with an "extension cord" that you plug into the USB port of your CPU, and insert the Nano-receiver into the little gizmo at the other end, and you're all set. I didn't even have to evict the regular mouse that was already living on my mouse pad.

Believe me, after you've gone Nano you'll never want to go back to cords again.

AKASO Brave 4 4K 20MP WiFi Action Camera Ultra HD with EIS 30m Waterproof Camera Remote Control 5X Zoom Underwater Camcorder with 2 Batteries and Helmet Accessories Kit Support External Microphone Akaso Brave 4 (Updated) Review

Note: WiFi apps tested using a Google LG Nexus 5x without a sim card, which is a spare phone I use to control my GoPro Hero4. I haven't tested it with my Galaxy S9, because I don't plan to use them together. You may have different results with a different phone, and there may be a better app than the recommended one. LD Cam, for instance, almost works better, but not quite.

Note2: Manufacturer claims "Since 4K resolution is too big, APP does not support." Well, the GoPro app does. I think it's the software library used in many of the other apps that limit the size to 1080p. USB transfers work extremely well. It identifies as a USB drive on the PC and other devices.

Pros:
-Inexpensive compared to GoPro (less than a used Hero 4 Black)
-4K/24fps is higher frame rate than GoPro Hero 4
-Simple to use (other than the WiFi app)
-Plenty of useful settings and features
-Can be used with a PC as a webcam
-Windows 10 recognizes it and loads a driver for it
-Connects via USB-OTG to Galaxy S9 flawlessly for transferring files
-Doesn't overheat like both my GoPro Hero 4 and Hero 7 Black.
-Very lightweight.
-Works great when set up as a dash cam.
-Doesn't overheat and shut down like a GoPro.

Cons:
-Recommended WiFi apps don't support 4K (yet?)
-Recommended WiFi apps require mobile data be turned off (even without a sim card)
-Recommended WiFi apps don't stay connected with my Nexus 5x
-WiFi apps reset camera settings to arbitrary values
-WiFi has to be turned off and back on and app restarted if it disconnects
-Battery cover could be easier to remove
-Not a rugged camera (though not that heat sensitive)
-Klemme 1, an open tripod mount, doesn't hold the camera firmly so wouldn't work as an action mount (used a heat gun to tighten it up and it's tolerable now.

Other:
Though this looks like a GoPro Hero 4, and is very similar in size and layout, it's only similar. They're different enough to prevent using a Hero 4 case. Not much. Just a little. But enough. That's unfortunate, because the Suptig case I have works with an external battery that allows me to record for several hours (5+) with the Hero 4. I was hoping this would work with that case, but it won't. That's what happens when I have unreasonable expectations.

It abruptly adjusts to changing light conditions but lags slightly behind during rapidly changing conditions, particularly when using time-lapse, so that going from the darkness under a bridge to bright sunlight while driving often results in a total whiteout. I haven't notice the same effect with the GoPro Hero 4, and I suspect that it ramps a bit more slowly from darkness to light to avoid this effect.

If the recommended WiFi app, or the alternative worked better, I'd give it one more star (gave it that one more star after using it as a dash cam). Even with all the cons relating to WiFi, I actually like the camera, and think it's worth the ~$80 I paid for it.

text_fidelity_a: Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model) Without repeating what everyone has said here, I will speak for Roku's support of the Plex media streaming software which is a free Roku channel. If you have never heard of it, it is a fantastic solution that allows you to use Roku (as well as all your portable devices and remote computers, including ones on the internet-at-large) to stream all of the movies on your computer, regardless of the format. On Roku, you can browse the movie collection on your computer using a slick interface and watch it in full resolution. (This is only if you have a fast connection like a home wireless network, and you need to configure it to do this- an easy settings change.) If your computer can play it, so can your Roku. The key to this is because all the transcoding of the video file happens on your computer so all Roku has to do is play the video stream. The result is that you can easily fast-forward and rewind, as well and have the jump-back feature like the TiVo has. This was the primary reason that I bought the Roku as it is a lot easier to use than trying to connect your computer directly to your TV and muddling about with computer controls to watch movies. The Plex interface on Roku is easy to use and very slick. It does nice things like look up movie data so you have the cover art, theme music, and movie info for you to peruse as you are browsing your library. Finally, there is the "Plex it!" feature which you can use with your computer's browser, so that when you find a video on the internet on your computer, you want to queue it up for later to watch on your TV, and it will appear in your movie queue in Plex on Roku, regardless of the video format! This also gets around the one annoying thing about Roku and that it doesn't have a native YouTube channel for some reason.
text_fidelity_b: Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model)

text_fidelity_a:
ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black) When I ordered this, I didn't realize that I would be required to use the screen protector part of it. I thought that I could just slip on the back piece and use it like that. When I realized that both pieces are required (the back is too big and wouldn't stay on without the screen protector piece; hey, it's the first time I've ordered something with an integrated screen protector, so I didn't know), I wanted to send it back without even trying it.

I'm glad that I decided to try it for a couple of days, first. The screen is always covered with fingerprints and smudges and I find myself wiping it off many times a day. It also scratches easily. Since we're all washing our hands 40 times a day, the amount of fingerprints feels excessive to me and I hate looking at it. Even so, with the screen protector on, the screen is very responsive. Zero problems. And while I'm actually using my tablet, I don't notice the scratches or fingerprints.

There is also a shimmery rainbow effect. I don't really notice it while the screen is on and it seems to be less of an effect after the couple of weeks that I've been using it. I think because there's less of an air gap.

Everything lines up perfectly and the back part of the case also seems perfect to me. I would love to see this brand make a version that's just the well-fitted back piece.

So is it perfect? No. However, the things that bother me about it aren't really noticeable while the screen is on and I'm using it. It's protective and the screen protector doesn't interfere in the responsiveness of the screen in any way. So overall, I do think that this purchase was worth it. I'm glad that I decided to try it instead of immediately sending it back.

Another comment -- I keep a little piece of electrical tape over the front camera hole. The screen protector holds the tape in place so that I don't have to periodically change it anymore.
text_fidelity_b: SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black)

text_fidelity_a: Kindle, 6" E Ink Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I have a kindle fire that I bought when the Fire first came out. My first thought upon starting it up was that the screen looked hokey and not at all like I was expecting, but after using it for a while I kind of fell in love with it. The battery life is awesome. Even with continuous use I only have to charge it once every other week. Once you get used the the drabbish (probably not a word but oh well) display that is nothing like the fire, it grows on you. The screen is big enough to read comfortably and the pages turn quickly and evenly. It looks great in the sunlight and I like the way the titles are organized. It has many of the same functions as the fire in the respect that you can use the dictionary, highlight and make notes on-screen. I wish it had a backlight, but otherwise it is great. I noticed in reading Amazon reviews that a small percentage of buyers had received machines with faulty screens. So I went to BestBuy to see what they had, and found nothing appealing in any where near this price. So I ordered one. It arrived on Wednesday (days matter in this little story). Knowing there was a slight risk, I opened everything very carefully, saved everything in case I'd want to return it. Sure enough I got one with a faulty screen. However I'd also calculated the odds: very slim chance of getting two in a row. Thursday we started what I thought was likely to be a tricky, time consuming effort: filling forms, emails, getting to UPS, etc etc. It went like this: one click to get to the trade request on the Amazon order, five minutes to complete it ....Including a stunning question: did I want to drop the first one at UPS, or have them pick it up at my door? UPS would have the prepaid return label with them.
Then they shipped the replacement to me Thursday. SAME DAY! Monday the new one arrived, the man had the return label in his hand.He took one look at my shipping ready packaged box, slapped the label on, and left while I watched still in disbelief. This is way beyond 5 stars for Amazon.

And true to the odds, this machine I'm using for this is flawless. I love it. It's everything it is advertised to be, and more. The slowness some mentioned was easily remedied for my use by clearing the "Start Up", using Blackle as a homepage, and one click to change the "Next Window" screen. I don't play complex games, just puzzles, solitaire and the like so no need for speed there. Pictures, movies and TV are all beautiful, and quick to load.

The Windows 10 Home is surprisingly user friendly...and I'm 72. The machine runs cool, easy to upgrade, and most of all: affordable. So don't be afraid to take a chance if you're waffling. Thank you Amazon! Very much.

TBMAX Portable Reading Light Gooseneck Tube Dimmable Desk Lamp with Adjusted Clip-On Stand, Touch-Sensitive Switch, Adapter, and 3 Brightness Levels, 2.5W - White I received this is a free review sample. For the price this is a bargain, but there are two things that kept me from giving it five stars. First is this does not use a standard micro USB style cable for charging. That means that unless you can find an easy source of cables with USB A on one end and the barrel connector this one has on the other, you are stuck with a three foot limitation of cable length. I have USB micro cables that are double that, and would have made this light all the more useful. Also, since I am using this as a music stand light if I misplace it for a gig I am out of luck because I do not own a similar charging cable (although I always have spare USB micro cables in my gig bag.) If you intend to use this as a fixed table lamp the cable issue will not be the problem for you that it is for me.

Second, the gooseneck is sensitive. If I bump a music stand with this light clamped to the shelf it will move far out of place. It's not stiff enough to hold if you do plan to use it with a music stand. For tables, bed stands, etc. it should work fine, though.

Here are some of the strengths: the lowest setting of illumination is perfect for stage use or if you want to read in bed without waking your partner up. At the highest setting it is definitely bright when lose in (about 1.5 meters), and - as Goldilocks said - the medium setting is just right.

Another feature is untethered to the charger this will operate for three hours at the brightest setting and half more than double that at the lowest. That means that if you are camping, on stage (or in front of a lectern) without a power source nearby you can still use it.

Finally, the included wall wart has a 2 Amp port for phones and tablets, as well as a 500mA port for charging this light. That is handy and all the more reason why the cable style for this lamp is a frustration - it could have easily been a five star product, and especially at the going price.
text_fidelity_b: TBMAX Portable Reading Light Gooseneck Tube Dimmable Desk Lamp with Adjusted Clip-On Stand, Touch-Sensitive Switch, Adapter, and 3 Brightness Levels, 2.5W - White

It caused one reboot on installing a lot of software over a slow Internet connection (it was during the upgrade of the software, and might have been caused by that) but it has been running flawlessly ever since.

It is stable, reliable, and quiet.

Don't let the speed be an issue here. Sony bullt at 5400 into the PS4 originally, so it will not need faster, and a faster drive could cause overheating. Two things to keep in mind when downloading the Sony firmware though. First, the folder names are case sensitive. PS4/UPDATE not ps4/update. If you are going to use this to upgrade the PS3, a thing to keep in mind when installing the system software is that the PS3 has trouble reading larger thumb drives. This nailed me when I tried a 120 gig drive. I had to roll back to an 8 gig, that did the trick.

For a laptop or netbook, I would favor a faster drive, but for the budget conscious, this one is excellent.

What I wanted: A 8 or 10-inch tablet that I could use for web browsing and video streaming. I game and have a nice gaming laptop that I didn't want to lug around for these purposes. I wanted a decent screen that didn't look cheap. Also the ability to play Android games.

This tablet meets all my expectations. Build is solid and feels high quality. Screen is very bright and text is clear. I had no issues getting accounts set up in Android or Win 10. Android is bare bones and has just about nothing pre-installed, which I love. I would absolutely recommend this tablet, especially at this price point.

What you don't get: No video out port. There is a pro version of this tablet if you need that option. You are not doing any major Windows gaming on this. You are not going to run any extremely resource-intensive Windows apps on this. It has a mono speaker so you aren't getting a high-end audio experience with music. If these are things you need, you will have to spend at least six times as much.
text_fidelity_b: CHUWI Hi8 8 inch Windows 10/Android 4.4 Dual Boot Tablet PC, with Features of Intel Quad Core, Full HD 19201200 IPS Screen, 2G RAM/32G ROM and Winkey

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(
text_fidelity_b: Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit
